title: The gut keeps its own time

scenes.tts: Mice born without one chloride channel have normal-looking pacemaker cells in the gut but no electrical slow waves. What does that channel do? The gut wall keeps its own time. The beat comes from branched cells between the muscle layers, the interstitial cells of Cajal, or I C C.
scenes.visual: A question: a gut wall with its pacemaker cells present, a flat rhythm trace, and a chloride channel crossed out; then the I C C light up as the source of the beat.
scenes.caption: Mice born without one chloride channel have normal-looking pacemaker cells in the gut but no electrical slow waves. What does that channel do? The gut wall keeps its own time. The beat comes from branched cells between the muscle layers, the interstitial cells of Cajal, or ICC.

scenes.tts: Record from a gut smooth muscle cell and you see slow waves, which are rhythmic depolarizations that last seconds. In the human stomach, pacemaker cells generate about three a minute. Isolated I C C show this rhythm, but isolated smooth muscle cells do not typically show it. In paired recordings from mouse gut muscle, the waves were larger in I C C. They reached the muscle passively, shrinking as they spread, so smooth muscle cannot regenerate them.
scenes.visual: A slow-wave trace drawn in a sketch; an isolated I C C keeps beating while an isolated muscle cell stays flat; in a pair, the large I C C wave shrinks as it reaches the muscle.
scenes.caption: Record from a gut smooth muscle cell and you see slow waves, which are rhythmic depolarizations that last seconds. In the human stomach, pacemaker cells generate about 3 a minute. Isolated ICC show this rhythm, but isolated smooth muscle cells do not typically show it. In paired recordings from mouse gut muscle, the waves were larger in ICC. They reached the muscle passively, shrinking as they spread, so smooth muscle cannot regenerate them.

scenes.tts: A slow wave is not an action potential, and it sets when the muscle can contract. A contraction follows only when a wave carries the muscle past threshold for calcium entry. Think of a metronome and a pianist. The metronome fixes the beat, and the pianist decides how loud each note is. Excitatory and inhibitory neurons, and hormones, set how strongly each wave couples to contraction.
scenes.visual: Beat marks fix the timing under a slow-wave trace; waves sit under a threshold line with no contraction; neurons and hormones lift the plateau over the threshold and contractions appear at the same beat.

scenes.tts: Small-intestinal muscle from Kit-mutant mice, with few myenteric I C C, lacked the slow waves of wild-type siblings. Mice lacking A N O one failed to develop slow waves, yet their I C C networks looked normal. So a calcium-activated chloride current is necessary for the rhythm, separately from building the network. It does not show that A N O one is the whole pacemaker. It describes neonatal mice, not adults or any human disorder.
scenes.visual: Three mouse panels: wild-type with I C C and slow waves, Kit-mutant with few I C C and a flat trace, A N O one null with normal I C C and a flat trace; hedge tags at the end.
scenes.caption: Small-intestinal muscle from Kit-mutant mice, with few myenteric ICC, lacked the slow waves of wild-type siblings. Mice lacking ANO1 failed to develop slow waves, yet their ICC networks looked normal. So a calcium-activated chloride current is necessary for the rhythm, separately from building the network. It does not show that ANO1 is the whole pacemaker. It describes neonatal mice, not adults or any human disorder.

scenes.tts: The enteric nervous system is the network of neurons in the gut wall. The myenteric plexus, between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers, mainly controls movement. In eighteen ninety-nine, Bayliss and Starling recorded loops of small intestine in anesthetized dogs. Distension of the wall caused contraction on the oral side and relaxation on the anal side, driving contents anally. The response persisted after the extrinsic nerves were cut, but was lost when conduction within the wall was blocked.
scenes.visual: Wall layers with the myenteric plexus; a gut loop as three blocks: the oral block narrows, the anal block widens, the bolus moves anally; cutting extrinsic nerves changes nothing, blocking conduction in the wall stops it.
